title: Jensen Huang resigns: how the Nvidia espionage reports unfolded
dek: In two weeks, a report that Nvidia’s founder was targeted by Chinese intelligence led to a board inquiry, another allegation, a share slide and his resignation.
seoTitle: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: timeline
bigLabel: Nvidia share price at the close on 20 November (US time), after Reuters reported an SEC accounting inquiry

glance.what: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on 12 November, two weeks after The New York Times reported that US intelligence found he had a close relationship with a Megaspeed executive they concluded was working for Beijing. Huang admitted infidelity, the board hired outside investigators, and a second alleged relationship, with a senior Nvidia executive, was reported on 11 November. On 19 November California's attorney general subpoenaed Nvidia over possible chip leaks to China and investor disclosures. On 20 November Reuters reported that SEC staff are examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia, and its shares fell 14%.
glance.why: Nvidia makes the chips behind most of the world’s AI and is one of the most valuable companies on earth. Its founder leaving under investigation raises questions about US–China chip security, who runs the company next, and what it means for investors.
glance.next: Huang said on 17 November he would return as CEO if the board asked; its chair said the same day that it does not intend to reinstate him. Huang is due to be questioned behind closed doors by three House committees on 1 December, per Axios. A new board committee will oversee national security and export controls, and the board is searching for a permanent CEO. No details of the reported SEC inquiry have been made public.

forYou: If you hold Nvidia shares or tech funds, expect volatility around the 17 November earnings and the CEO search. No outlet has reported that Huang broke any law or that Nvidia secrets were lost; the espionage claims are allegations that China denies, and the second relationship is reported, not confirmed.

upcoming.label: 1 Dec
upcoming.text: Huang's closed-door interview with three House committees (per Axios)

upcoming.label: 2 Dec
upcoming.text: Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter's interview

next: Any response from Nvidia or the SEC to the reported accounting inquiry; Huang's closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December and general counsel Tim Teter's on 2 December (per Axios); a public Senate Banking Committee hearing with Huang, date not yet set; the board's search for a permanent CEO; investigations by the board, California's attorney general, Congress and the Justice and Commerce departments.

events.title: New York Times report: Huang targeted by Chinese intelligence
events.summary: US intelligence agencies found Huang had developed a close relationship with an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, one of Nvidia’s biggest Southeast Asian customers, whom US officials concluded was gathering information for Beijing. Officials did not believe Huang knew. Nvidia said the interactions were a normal part of his job. China called the claims baseless smears.

events.title: House committee chairs ask Huang for a closed-door briefing
events.summary: Three Republican House committee chairs ask Huang to brief them on 18 November about his contacts with the Megaspeed executive and Nvidia’s protections against espionage, with a reply due by 11 November. The letter comes a day after midterms in which Republicans lost control of Congress.

events.title: Incoming Democratic majority signals its own questions
events.summary: Bloomberg reports that the new Democratic majority in Congress is set to demand answers from Nvidia on keeping its AI chips out of China. The new Congress sits from 3 January.

events.title: Board opens independent investigation; Huang admits infidelity
events.summary: A committee of independent directors with outside counsel will review the reports. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and that it has confidence in Huang, who stays CEO. In a message to staff, Huang says he was unfaithful to his wife and will cooperate fully. President Trump calls him an honourable man and says he has not discussed the matter with him.

events.title: Shares slide; China rejects the claims
events.summary: Nvidia falls as much as 8% in early trading before recovering to about 4% down, while rivals AMD and Broadcom rise. China’s Foreign Ministry calls the allegations unsubstantiated. Huang pulls out of an AI industry CEO forum.

events.title: Former US attorney and Wachtell Lipton hired to run the inquiry
events.summary: The board names Joon Kim, a former acting US Attorney, and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the independent investigation. Nvidia’s losses since Monday reach close to $500 billion in market value, according to NBC News.
events.differs: NBC News puts the fall at more than 10% since Monday; CNN reported the shares down over 5% for the week on 11 November.

events.title: New report alleges a second relationship, with a senior Nvidia executive
events.summary: The New York Times reports, citing five employees, that Huang is also suspected of a relationship with a married executive who reports directly to him. Nvidia has rules discouraging relationships between managers and subordinates. This is a reported allegation; Nvidia’s response had not been published in the coverage we reviewed. Analysts have started asking whether Huang could be forced to step aside, with no public succession plan.

events.title: Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO
events.summary: After a board meeting on Wednesday night, Nvidia says its co-founder has stepped down as chief executive. Chief financial officer Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis, and venture investor Harvey C. Jones becomes the company’s first board chair. The board is reported to be looking at outside candidates for the permanent role. Investigations by the FBI and Congress, and a shareholder class-action lawsuit, continue.
events.differs: Yahoo Finance reports the shares fell as much as 13% before recovering; StockTitan had them down 4.5% by early afternoon New York time.

events.title: Shares fall 4% on the day he resigns
events.summary: Nvidia closes down about 4%, taking its fall from the 6 October record high to 30.5%, according to CNN. Bloomberg, citing Vanda Research, reports retail investors bought a record $111 million of Nvidia shares in the first 30 minutes of trading.

events.title: Huang agrees to appear before Congress
events.summary: Huang agrees to appear voluntarily before the relevant House committees, CNN reports. Senators from both parties call the case troubling, and some want Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify too. Nvidia says its product roadmap and customer commitments continue.

events.title: Reports: the board pushed him out
events.summary: A person familiar with the matter tells CNBC the board decided to oust Huang after the report of a second alleged affair. Bloomberg, via The Japan Times, reports he will no longer have ties to Nvidia, and that an outside firm is helping find CEO candidates. Rival AMD's shares are up nearly 17% this week.
events.differs: Nvidia's statement calls it a resignation; CNBC's source says the board decided to remove him.

events.title: Lawyers, a chip-smuggling probe and a CEO search
events.summary: Bloomberg reports Huang has hired the law firm Paul Weiss, and that the Justice Department is looking into the woman at the centre of the case over possible links to chip smuggling. Kress keeps her CFO role while the board considers inside and outside candidates. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick will appear before the Senate Banking Committee, and Fortune reports Huang keeps a 3.6% stake.

events.title: Market value falls below $4 trillion
events.summary: Nvidia shares fall 2% to close at $162.85, ending the week down about 12%, and its market value closes below $4 trillion. It was worth as much as $5.75 trillion on 5 October. HSBC downgrades the stock to Hold and cuts its price target to $170 from $365, a day after Bernstein cut its target to $200 from $400.

events.title: Who might replace Huang: Trump backs Tim Cook; other names floated
events.summary: On Thursday, hours after the resignation, President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that "there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple." Nvidia and Apple had not replied to requests for comment, per Newsweek. Business Insider reports that the Financial Times said Nvidia had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, though it is not certain he would be offered the job or accept it, and that a person familiar with the matter told Semafor Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is being considered. Analysts have also named Nvidia's Ian Buck and interim CEO Colette Kress. Nvidia has not named any candidates.
events.status: Stated · Trump; candidate names Reported or analyst views

events.title: Reports say Huang is discussing a comeback; Bessent calls for an outside CEO
events.summary: The Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter, that Jensen Huang has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning as Nvidia's chief executive, according to Reuters and The Next Web. Two Nvidia investors, Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides' Gavin Baker, posted a letter to the board on X urging a slow search for a successor that includes "the potential return of Jensen Huang", The Next Web reports. The same day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures" that Nvidia needs a "dramatic shakeup" and should look outside the company for a new CEO. "If this were a bank and they hadn't complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now and a lot of the executives would be removed," he said, per Fortune. Fortune reports he also questioned whether Nvidia used "seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings." Nvidia did not immediately respond, per Fortune.

events.title: Board reportedly not considering Huang's return; Trump says he 'would not mind'
events.summary: Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to CNBC, the New York Post and Fox News on Monday (US time). CNBC's source said the board is focused on its investigation into Huang, led by the law firm Wachtell Lipton, and is not in talks with him. "There is just no realistic path," one person told the Post. Nvidia has not commented. The same day, President Donald Trump said of a return: "I would certainly not mind seeing that," adding that Huang had "learned a big lesson". Of the Megaspeed executive at the centre of the reports, he said: "I don't know that she's a spy at all. Nobody's proven that." An online petition to reinstate Huang has about 180,000 signatures, per CNBC. Fox News reports that Megaspeed says the executive left the company in 2025.
events.status: Reported · CNBC, New York Post, Fox News (anonymous sources); Stated · Trump
events.differs: Trump's words are quoted slightly differently: "I would certainly not mind seeing that" (CNBC, Fox News) and "I would not mind that" (New York Post).

sources.name: New York Post via Yahoo Finance

events.title: Shares fall 4% on the eve of earnings
events.summary: Nvidia shares closed at $156.14 on Monday, down 4.12%, per the Motley Fool, leaving the company's market value at about $3.92 trillion. The Independent also reports a drop of more than 4% and says Nvidia has lost about $800 billion in market value since details of Huang's relationship emerged. The wider Nasdaq index fell 2.49%. The Motley Fool links the fall to new US limits on access to advanced AI chips, analysts lowering their price targets and uncertainty over the leadership change. The Independent reports that more than 190,000 people have signed a petition to reinstate Huang; the petition's figures for Nvidia employees and shareholders who signed are self-reported and not checked.

events.title: Justice and Commerce departments confirm a joint probe of Megaspeed
events.summary: The US Justice Department and Commerce Department said in a joint statement that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud-computing company at the centre of the Huang reports, and would pursue it to the "fullest extent of the law" for "any criminal conduct that may have occurred", per ABC News. ABC reports Commerce's inquiry began in 2024 and that Nvidia put Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list in June 2025. Megaspeed has not been charged with any crime.
events.status: Confirmed · DOJ and Commerce, via ABC News

events.title: Huang says he would be 'honored' to return as CEO if the board wants him
events.summary: In his first public statement since resigning, posted on X and sent to news outlets, Huang said he had "made serious mistakes" in his personal life and was committed to cooperating with the board's independent investigation. He said employees, investors, partners and customers had called for him to come back, and that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if the board decides that is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America. CBS News, citing a person familiar with the board's thinking, reports the board is not interested in reinstating him in any role.

events.title: First results without Huang: revenue doubles; board chair says Huang won't return
events.summary: Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for August–October, up 103% from a year earlier, in its first results under interim CEO Colette Kress. Data centre sales, mostly AI chips, were $107.6 billion. Profit was $65.3 billion. Nvidia expects about $130 billion in sales next quarter, assuming no data centre chip sales to China. "Our momentum is real," Kress said. On the earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said "the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO", per Constellation Research; CBS News, citing a person familiar with the board's thinking, also reports the board is against his return. Shares fell 0.44% in regular trading, then rose nearly 3% after hours, per CBS News.
events.differs: Reports differ on the after-hours rise: CBS News says nearly 3% (to $159.60), Reuters says as much as 3%, and StockTitan gives 4.55% at 6:23 pm ET.

events.title: Board sets up a national security and export control committee; Huang to be questioned on 1 December
events.summary: Nvidia's board created a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to oversee the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risks. It is chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, with directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri, and will meet at least quarterly. Separately, Axios reports Huang will sit for a closed-door, transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China select committees on 1 December, and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter on 2 December. This is not a public hearing.
events.differs: Earlier reports said Huang's appearance was expected before Thanksgiving (26 November); Axios and ABC News give 1 December. Axios says its report may be updated.

events.title: Shares fall about 3% the day after results
events.summary: Nvidia shares closed down 2.89% on Wednesday, per StockTitan, giving up their after-hours gain from the night before. Yahoo Finance reports it was the fifth day of losses in a row, and that the strong results did not outweigh worries about Huang's departure.
events.differs: The Motley Fool's quote shows −2.9% at $150.96; Yahoo Finance's page showed −2.68% before the final close.

events.title: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia
events.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia, his office said on Thursday, per AP and CBS News. A subpoena is a legal order to hand over documents or answer questions. The state wants to know whether Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information may have reached China, and whether the company misled investors and the public, per AP; CBS adds whether it broke state law. "Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta said. "Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation." Nvidia did not immediately respond, per AP. A subpoena is not a finding of wrongdoing.

events.title: Reuters: SEC staff examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia; shares fall 14%
events.summary: Two people briefed on the matter told Reuters that enforcement staff at the SEC, the US markets regulator, are examining "potential accounting issues" at Nvidia. Reuters could not find out when the inquiry began or which issues it covers. The Wall Street Journal had reported an SEC probe on 17 November without saying what it focused on. The SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not immediately respond, per Reuters. An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing, and many end without action. Nvidia shares closed down 14.01% at $125.53, per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes, the worst day since January 2025, per CappNotes. Reuters, citing LSEG data, says shares were already down more than 6% before its report.

events.title: Huang to testify in public before the Senate Banking Committee; no date set
events.summary: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, a spokesperson for its chairman, Senator Tim Scott, told Politico on 17 November. Scott told CNBC on 18 November that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had agreed to appear and that he hoped to hold the hearing "before Christmas". His letters had asked for Huang on 3 December and Lutnick on 10 December. On 20 November Scott's spokesperson confirmed the testimony will be public, CNBC reported, with no date set. Whether witnesses will testify under oath had not been decided, per Streamline. This is separate from Huang's closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December.
events.status: Stated · Senate Banking Committee chairman's office (via Politico and CNBC)

events.title: California's attorney general says his inquiry covers civil and criminal state law
events.summary: A day after his office subpoenaed Nvidia, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the inquiry looks at whether Nvidia or former CEO Jensen Huang gave the public false information about chip sales to China. He said state laws that ban misleading investors and the public include "both civil and criminal clauses", per Zhitong via Longbridge. Bonta said the inquiry is at a preliminary stage and no conclusions have been reached. An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. Neither report includes a response from Nvidia.

events.title: New York Times also reports the SEC inquiry; questions over how Nvidia reports sales by region
events.summary: The New York Times reported on Saturday that the SEC is investigating Nvidia's accounting, citing people briefed on the confidential inquiry, per AFP. AFP says the inquiry is at an early stage and could end without charges, and that it is unclear whether it concerns a change in how Nvidia reports sales by region or the Huang affair. Last year Nvidia stopped reporting regional sales by customers' billing address and began using where customers are headquartered, which removed Singapore from the breakdown; Nvidia said this better reflects its revenue, per Reuters. The Financial Times had reported that Singapore made up almost half of global revenue before the change, Reuters says. Nvidia did not respond and the SEC declined to comment. Nvidia shares fell more than 20% over the week, per AFP. Separately, President Trump said: "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance"; the board chair has ruled out Huang's return.
events.status: Reported · New York Times, Reuters (via AFP and Korea Times); Stated · Trump

heroTitle: NYT joins Reuters in reporting an SEC inquiry into Nvidia's accounting
heroDek: The inquiry is at an early stage, per AFP; it is unclear whether it concerns how Nvidia reports sales by region or the Huang affair. Shares fell more than 20% last week. Huang is due before three House committees on 1 December.
